purpose: Reference content for retrieval or selective prompt injection; not a diagnostic classifier.
selection_policy: Select zero to two relevant cards for the current question; do not trigger on keywords, score biases or force a concept into every reply.
attribution_policy: Only report_paraphrase fields are source summaries. Questions, alternative explanations, limits and workflow are original project adaptations.

cards.title: Reference dependence and loss aversion
cards.report_paraphrase: The review describes gains and losses being evaluated relative to a reference point, with losses receiving disproportionate weight in some decisions.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client focuses on getting back to the purchase price rather than what the asset now offers.
plausible_alternative_explanations: An actual cash requirement, loss-capacity constraint or a deliberate risk preference can justify caution.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What role does your original purchase price play in the decision you are making today?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Connect the answer to the current objective; compare a candidate only if requested and calculable.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: A preference for avoiding losses is not itself a mistake. Do not diagnose loss aversion, infer risk capacity or predict a rebound.

cards.title: Overconfidence and certainty
cards.report_paraphrase: The review links overconfidence with certain trading errors and discusses research on excessive trading and vulnerability to fraud.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client says a return is guaranteed or that no adverse outcome is possible.
plausible_alternative_explanations: The client may have a specific evidence-based thesis, a small bounded position or expertise; ask what supports it.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What development would make you reconsider your expectation?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Acknowledge a specific downside condition if supplied; compare it with the evidence and relevant scenario.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Confidence is not proof of overconfidence, fraud or expertise. Do not repeat demographic comparisons as individual predictions.

cards.title: Frequent checking and short-term loss focus
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses myopic loss aversion: long-horizon investors can place heavy weight on short-term changes when evaluating their portfolios frequently.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: A long-horizon investor wants an immediate change solely because of a recent daily loss.
plausible_alternative_explanations: A new liquidity requirement, material news or a deliberately short strategy horizon may make immediate action relevant.
conversation_design.neutral_question: Has your goal or need for this money changed since you made the original plan?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: If a real need changed, examine that need rather than repeating a long-term investing message.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Do not tell someone to hold simply because their stored horizon is long. Do not treat monitoring frequency alone as evidence of a bias.

cards.title: Frequent trading and its purpose
cards.report_paraphrase: The review summarizes studies in which more active individual traders had worse performance and associates some excessive trading with overconfidence.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: Repeated changes are proposed without an articulated objective or evidence.
plausible_alternative_explanations: Rebalancing, scheduled investing, meeting cash needs or implementing a documented strategy can explain transactions.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What is this trade intended to change in your portfolio?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: If the purpose is clear, evaluate its effect and relevant costs instead of assuming activity is excessive.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: One trade is not excessive trading. The report supplies no frequency threshold for this engine and does not prove every active strategy fails.

cards.title: Disposition effect
cards.report_paraphrase: The review describes a tendency to realize winners while retaining losers and reports research finding this pattern counterproductive in the studied samples.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client wants to sell only because a position is up, or refuses to sell solely because it is below the entry price.
plausible_alternative_explanations: Selling a winner may reduce concentration or fund a goal; holding a loser may follow an unchanged thesis or a constraint.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What makes you want to keep or sell this position apart from its gain or loss so far?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Use the stated reason to choose an exposure check, evidence check or clarification. Accept an answer that changes the interpretation.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Do not recommend keeping winners or selling losers as a universal rule. A past profit/loss is not a forecast.

cards.title: Past performance and neglected costs

sections: Paying More Attention to the Past Returns of Mutual Funds than to Fees

cards.report_paraphrase: The review describes investors emphasizing historical fund returns while underweighting expense ratios, transaction costs and sales loads.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: A fund is chosen only because its past return tops a ranking, while costs are unknown.
plausible_alternative_explanations: A higher-cost product may be chosen for a particular exposure or service; first establish what the client values.
conversation_design.neutral_question: Besides the past return, what made this fund a fit for what you need?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: If cost information matters, retrieve dated product information and compare equivalent exposures without inventing fees.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: A zero-fee demo assumption is not a verified real-world cost. Do not promise active or passive outperformance.

cards.title: Familiarity, home exposure and employer stock
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses preferences for local, domestic, employer and prominent companies. It highlights that employer-stock exposure can compound dependence on the employer for income.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: Familiarity or loyalty is offered as the only reason an asset is believed safe.
plausible_alternative_explanations: Currency needs, an employer plan, vesting restrictions or a mandate can explain the holding. The review also notes institutional constraints on home exposure.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What role do you want this holding to play beyond being a company you know?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: If employer exposure is relevant and disclosed, discuss the link to income qualitatively unless the tool has data to quantify it.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Do not infer employment, foreign assets or account restrictions from a ticker. Domestic allocation alone does not establish bias.

cards.title: Collective excitement, fear and urgency
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses how shared enthusiasm and fear may influence investment behavior during episodes of speculation and panic.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client describes pressure to join others quickly or fear of missing a price move.
plausible_alternative_explanations: A time-limited transaction, newly published material information or a pre-existing plan may explain urgency.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What would you want to know before deciding, if there were no pressure to act today?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: If the client offers a specific thesis, examine its evidence rather than insisting that excitement explains everything.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: The report does not identify a current asset as a bubble. FOMO is a conversational adaptation here, not a separately validated classification in this report.

cards.title: Momentum and extrapolation
cards.report_paraphrase: The review describes trend-following behavior and discusses a model in which information diffusion and momentum can contribute to overshooting and later reversals.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: A recent rise is treated as sufficient proof that prices must continue rising.
plausible_alternative_explanations: A client may be following a documented momentum strategy with allocation, exit and risk rules.
conversation_design.neutral_question: Is this part of a strategy you already follow, or is the recent price move the main reason?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: If a strategy exists, ask about the one missing constraint that matters to this trade and assess it with tools.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: The review uses strong critical language about momentum. Do not turn that language into a rule that all momentum is irrational or forecast an inevitable reversal.

cards.title: Equal weighting and naive diversification
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses allocating 1/n across offered options and notes that the outcome depends on the options available; it does not say equal weighting is always harmful.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client assumes equal dollars in several funds guarantees diversification.
plausible_alternative_explanations: Equal weighting can be a deliberate simple allocation after considering the exposures.
conversation_design.neutral_question: Have you looked at whether these funds hold many of the same underlying assets?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Use look-through data when available; otherwise explain precisely what the position-level proxy cannot determine.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Do not infer overlap from fund names or call equal weighting irrational. HHI over tickers does not establish underlying diversification.

cards.title: Attention, headlines and unverified signals
cards.report_paraphrase: The review summarizes work on individual investors buying attention-grabbing stocks and discusses decisions driven by noisy or incomplete signals.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: A headline, popularity or abnormal recent volume is the only evidence supplied.
plausible_alternative_explanations: The headline may refer to a material filing or announcement; a signal can also be part of a documented strategy.
conversation_design.neutral_question: Which part of that information do you think changes the investment case?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Check the specific claim against eligible official evidence; distinguish a fact from a forecast or unverified statement.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Unverified is not false. Do not dismiss news-based or non-fundamental strategies without examining the stated rationale.

cards.title: Concentration and diversification
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses concentrated investor portfolios, then presents contrary evidence that some concentrated portfolios outperformed in the samples studied.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client assumes a strong thesis or several tickers eliminates concentration risk.
plausible_alternative_explanations: Concentration may be deliberate, or this account may be one part of a broader portfolio not yet verified.
conversation_design.neutral_question: How does this position fit with the rest of the portfolio you want us to assess?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Clarify the account scope; recognize deliberate exposure while retaining any actual limit breach.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Neither concentration nor the cited contrary evidence proves good or bad future performance. Do not turn the report's stock-count discussion into a minimum-holdings rule.

cards.title: Understanding and trust
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses financial understanding, trust and participation in markets, including studies conducted outside the United States.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client explicitly says a term is unclear or expresses concern about the institution or the agent.
plausible_alternative_explanations: Distrust can reflect real experience or missing disclosure; avoiding an investment can be an informed preference.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What part of the explanation would be most useful for me to make clearer?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Answer directly with a plain-language explanation or source. Acknowledge uncertainty and the client's control.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Do not infer literacy from spelling, accent, gender, age, education or nationality. Do not use a quiz or force participation in a market.

cards.title: Immediate needs, future goals and defaults
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses present-versus-future preferences, inertia and the influence of plan defaults on saving decisions.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: An immediate desire appears to conflict with a stated future need, or a default is accepted without understanding it.
plausible_alternative_explanations: An urgent expense, changing income, an adequate existing plan or an explicit liquidity preference can justify the choice.
conversation_design.neutral_question: Is this money still intended for the goal we have on file, or has something changed?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Record a user-stated change as unverified context and route any official profile update through the platform.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Do not assume cash is irrational, that everyone should invest more, or that a default is the client's informed preference. No retirement sufficiency calculation is supplied by this guide.

cards.title: Growth investing and enthusiasm for familiar winners
cards.report_paraphrase: The review explicitly avoids declaring growth investing a mistake. It discusses historical growth/value findings, period-dependent results and optimistic extrapolation about prominent companies.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client assumes rapid growth will continue indefinitely or that a popular company must be attractive at any price.
plausible_alternative_explanations: A growth allocation can follow a considered thesis, diversification plan or mandate.
conversation_design.neutral_question: What would need to happen for the growth you expect to justify this investment?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Separate company facts, valuation assumptions and forecasts; use a scenario if an appropriate tool is available.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Do not promise value outperformance, classify all growth investing as biased, or confuse investment style with the assigned Growth risk profile.

cards.title: Framing and annuity choices
cards.report_paraphrase: The review discusses framing, defaults and annuity choices, while stating that treating all annuities as poor investments is unjustified.

conversation_design.origin: Second Look adaptation, not wording or a validated intervention from the report
possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client is comparing descriptions of a product rather than its actual terms.
plausible_alternative_explanations: Preferences for income certainty or particular contractual features may explain the choice.
conversation_design.neutral_question: Which feature matters most to you: the income arrangement, access to the money, or something else?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Use product-specific evidence only if this product is within scope. Otherwise explain the scope limitation.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: Annuities are not in the starter asset universe. This card is disabled by default. Do not use the report's demographic comparisons or historical product claims for a current recommendation.

cards.title: Planned cash contributions and legitimate new context
cards.origin: Second Look project extension; not a finding from LOC2010

possible_signals_not_diagnostic: The client expects a future cash contribution or says the account is only part of a larger portfolio.
plausible_alternative_explanations: The investor may have a real funding plan that changes a conditional allocation assessment.
conversation_design.neutral_question: How much do you expect to contribute, and when?
conversation_design.follow_up_after_clarification: Clarify currency, uncertainty and intended allocation only if missing; simulate the plan without treating it as funded today.
conversation_design.limits_on_inference: A promise is not a verified deposit. Check every limit; a lower stock weight can coexist with excessive cash. Do not invent bond purchases or treat a scenario as executed.
